methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ACSL is a public-stage drone and autonomous systems company listed on the Tokyo exchange, founded by Kenzo Nonami. The valuation landscape for this sector consists of six private comparables—Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air among them—with no public peers identified in the same narrow segment.

Peer-median triangulation is not applicable here due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Drones & Autonomous sector. While five same-sector peers exist globally, none satisfy the filtering criteria of matching stage, proximity, or valuation tier required for a reliable median benchmark. A broad all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the specialized capital structures and growth profiles in autonomous systems.

The absence of a robust public peer set and the heterogeneity of private financing rounds limit conventional multiples-based approaches. Any valuation synthesis for ACSL would require either (1) revenue or EBITDA-based exit comps from the private peer group, (2) discounted cash flow analysis grounded in regulatory and commercialization timelines specific to autonomous systems, or (3) explicit scenario weighting across development-stage risk factors. Without the specific financial metrics or transaction data for named comparables, a quantitative range cannot be supported by this dataset alone. Further diligence on peer-round economics and ACSL's own financials is prerequisite.
